subject: Request: temporary rate-tier bridge for week-of-promo (true-up & PO)
messages:
From: Kyle Turner <kyle@brightcart.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary rate-tier bridge for week-of-promo

Hi Olga,

Quick one — we have a planned marketing promo for the week of July 4 that will spike GraphQL/assist calls ~3x over our baseline for about 48 hours (peak expected: 36–48 hours starting 2027-07-03 08:00 UTC). Forecast attached (promo_traffic_forecast.xlsx).

We need a short-lived increase to our rate tier / throttle to avoid degraded UX. Can Redwood provision a temporary step-up to cover ~1.8M tokens/day (ballpark) and tell us:
- What the overage/step-up pricing would look like for a 48-hour window
- Whether you offer a discount or a fixed short-term rate if we provide a PO for the incremental capacity
- How billing/true-up would be handled (separate invoice vs addendum to our existing contract)

Two constraints: we need final terms by EOD Wednesday 2027-06-23 so procurement can issue a PO, and we prefer a straightforward charge we can reconcile to our monthly invoice.

Thanks — Kyle
Kyle Turner
Head of Platform, BrightCart
kyle@brightcart.com

Attachment: promo_traffic_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Kyle Turner <kyle@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-tier bridge for week-of-promo

Kyle — thanks for the forecast and timeline. We can support a short window uplift, and we have two pragmatic options that should meet procurement timelines: 

Option A — Ephemeral headroom (fastest):
- 48-hour temporary throttle step-up to the requested cap
- Overrun billed at 1.4x your standard overrun rate (applies only to the incremental capacity)
- No long-term contract change; invoice issued as a separate line item with same payment terms

Option B — PO-backed temporary commit (preferred economics):
- If BrightCart issues a PO for a 3-month incremental commit (covers the promo and headroom afterwards), we can reduce the overrun multiplier to 1.1x and provide a one-time 12% discount on the incremental units for the promo window
- Billing: addendum to the existing invoice or a standalone invoice — your choice; we'll include a pro-rata true-up in the following month to reconcile actual usage vs PO

Actionable items: if you can push a PO by EOD 2027-06-23 we can lock Option B. I attached a short quote (temp-pricing-quote.pdf) showing both paths and the back-of-envelope costs.

Cc'ing Marissa (sales ops) to surface billing/PO steps and Karthik for the serving/ops confirmation on perf risk and canary cadence.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Attachment: temp-pricing-quote.pdf (PDF)
From: Kyle Turner <kyle@brightcart.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:19:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-tier bridge for week-of-promo

Hi Olga — thanks for the quick breakdown. Option B looks attractive, but procurement pushed back on the sticker. Two asks from our side: 

1) Can Redwood improve the PO-backed discount to 20% on the incremental units for the promo window? That brings the incremental cost in line with our margin assumptions for the campaign.
2) We need the surge billed as an addendum on the same monthly invoice (not a separate vendor invoice) so our accounts payable can net it against the committed spend.

I've attached the draft PO to speed things up (BrightCart_PO_0704.pdf) — if you can accept with redlines by EOD Wednesday I can have it approved.

—Kyle

Attachment: BrightCart_PO_0704.pdf (draft PO)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kyle Turner <kyle@brightcart.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-tier bridge for week-of-promo

Kyle — appreciate the draft. Two quick notes from billing/legal ops: 

- We can accept adding the surge as an addendum to the existing monthly invoice, provided the PO references the primary contract and nets to the same payment terms. That keeps AP happy.
- Regarding the discount: 20% is larger than our standard short-term concession for unscheduled spikes. We can get to 18% if BrightCart can sign the three-month incremental commit in the PO and include a mutual SLA clause limiting peak sustained throughput to the agreed uplift for the 48-hour window. That gives us runway to reallocate capacity without exposure.

True-up mechanics we propose:
- Promo usage billed against the incremental PO first; any bona fide oversubscribe beyond the PO will be billed at 1.15x the incremental rate (reduced from 1.4x due to commit)
- Any unused portion of the three-month incremental commit will be credited pro-rata at month end

If that matches procurement's requirements we'll produce an addendum and updated cost schedule by EOD Wednesday. Marissa

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kyle Turner <kyle@brightcart.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-tier bridge for week-of-promo

Kyle / team — quick technical confirmation from infra: we can safely open an elevated throttle for the 48-hour window with a conservative canary rollout (first 10% of traffic, 30-minute ramp) and automated fallback on error rate/latency thresholds. A couple of suggestions to keep unit costs down: 

- Enable prefix caching for the most common prompt templates (reduces repeat token generation)
- Shorten KV cache retention on ephemeral instances post-event to free memory
- If acceptable to BrightCart, we can apply a soft cap on single-request token-length (recommend 2,000 tokens) for the promo to avoid pathological outliers

I'll coordinate with ops to schedule the canary on 2027-07-03 07:00 UTC so the promo start has an hour of validation. From a billing standpoint we'll tag all promo-related requests so the true-up maps cleanly to the PO.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Kyle Turner <kyle@brightcart.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-tier bridge for week-of-promo

All — we can take 18% and the 3-month incremental PO path. Attached is the signed PO (BrightCart_PO_0704_signed.pdf). Please route final addendum to procurement@brightcart.com and bill it as an addendum on our July invoice. Please confirm the canary schedule (we're good for 07:00 UTC on 2027-07-03).

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Appreciate the caching suggestions — we'll enable prefix caching and cap request length as suggested.

—Kyle

Attachment: BrightCart_PO_0704_signed.pdf (signed PO)
